title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
desc: Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Despite rapid growth in publicly available dermatology images, the field lacks quantitative indicators to measure whether new datasets expand clinical coverage or merely replicate what is already known. Existing collections are widely assumed to be biased, yet the scale and topography of these gaps have remained unquantified, leaving the community without a road map for strategic data acquisition. Here, we show, by unifying 1.1 million images from 29 public datasets into a queryable semantic atlas, that the global archive is markedly skewed and increasingly redundant: darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick V–VI) constitute only 11.0% of images, pediatric patients only 2.3%, and informational novelty has plateaued despite exponential growth, revealing where targeted data acquisition is most needed. The authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

title: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
desc: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously.
